transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m worried about how it feels once I start picking at food late at night. I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then my hand just keeps going back. It feels like I’m not really making the decision anymore.
When this happens late at night, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yeah. Some nights after work, I’ll have several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left. I’m standing there in the kitchen telling myself I’m just finishing leftovers, but it ends up being a lot.
During those late-night eating episodes, do you feel unable to stop eating once you’ve started?
Yeah. I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but I keep reaching for more anyway. It feels like I’m not really the one deciding to stop.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to undo the eating?
No, I don’t make myself throw up afterward.
After those episodes, do you ever use laxatives to try to undo the eating?
I’m not sure what you mean by laxatives. I don’t really know about that.
After you eat like that, do you ever take laxatives to try to get rid of the food or prevent weight gain?
No, I don’t take anything like that after I eat.
After you eat like that, do you ever skip meals or go without eating to make up for it?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to whether I do that.
Do these eating episodes upset you a lot?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about how much they upset me.
When these eating episodes happen, do they make you feel very upset or distressed?
I don’t know if I’d say very upset. I haven’t really paid attention to how I feel afterward.
Do you feel very upset or distressed about these eating episodes?
I can’t really say. I haven’t noticed feeling especially distressed about them.
Do these eating episodes bother you a lot?
I mean, I know they happen, but I wouldn’t say they bother me a lot. I just haven’t really focused on it that way.
After one of these late-night eating episodes, do you intentionally skip your next meal to make up for it?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I skip the next meal because of it.
How often do these late-night eating episodes happen?
For the past several months, it’s been most weeks, at least once. Usually it’s when there are a lot of leftovers and everybody else has gone to bed.
Do these late-night eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?
I don’t know if I’d call it a lot of distress. I haven’t really thought about it that way.
When this happens, do you eat much more food than most people would eat in the same situation?

Yeah, some nights I do. After work I can eat several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left. I’m usually just standing in the kitchen, telling myself I’m cleaning up the leftovers.
After one of these eating episodes, do you ever exercise a lot on purpose to make up for it?
No, I don’t really exercise afterward to make up for it.
After one of these late-night eating episodes, do you purposely go without eating for a long time to make up for it?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I skip eating for a long time afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you feel disgusted with yourself or very guilty?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to how I feel afterward, honestly.
When these late-night episodes happen, do you eat an amount of food that most people would consider unusually large for that time?

Yeah, some nights it’s a lot. I’ll have several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left. I’m usually standing there in the kitchen, telling myself I’m just finishing the leftovers.
Do you wake up from sleep and then eat during the night?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I’m waking up from sleep first or just staying up and eating.
